A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM-R1 and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. The complete documents support comparison, including matching v1's main-text failure ablations to Appendix A.1-A.2 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAM-R1 benchmark results, component ablations, training behavior and qualitative segmentation outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds segmentation failure cases and a 3k-versus-10k training-data experiment in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5VL-7B and frozen SAM2-Large framework, tiered segmentation reward, format rewards, asymmetric clipping and token-level loss normalization remain unchanged. The added appendix experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RefCOCOg training and evaluation on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, ReasonSeg and LISA-Grounding. The added training-size comparison and ReasonSeg-val failure cases do not introduce another dataset, task or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: v2 removes Qwen2.5VL-3B+SAM2 from the ReasonSeg comparison in Table 1. Other comparator sets are retained. Seg-Zero* becomes Seg-Zero-7B* with identical scores, indicating a clarified label rather than an added comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a 10k-training-sample condition alongside the existing 3k condition. The previously reported splits, image resizing, metrics, backbone and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; this is an additional sample-size experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 and Figure 5 add three cases examining incomplete segmentation, missed instances and over-segmentation. Appendix A.4 tests sensitivity to training-data quantity. Existing threshold and algorithmic ablations remain unchanged, while the KL and negative-point failure studies are relocated to Appendix A.1-A.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation across repeated training runs, seed variability, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new training-size comparison also reports point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds 10k-condition scores: ReasonSeg val/test cIoU of 55.5/53.9 versus 55.8/54.3 at 3k, and RefCOCO/+/g scores of 79.9/75.3/73.5 versus 79.2/74.7/73.1. These are additional settings, not revised same-setting scores. Retained benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. v2 also adds Figure 5 failure outputs, replaces Figure 1's illustrative example and removes the Qwen2.5VL-3B+SAM2 result row.

T1.justification: Equations 1-5 retain the same advantage normalization, GRPO and modified objectives, KL expression and tiered reward definition. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about SAM-guided reinforcement learning, fine-grained rewards, the tailored optimization objective and strong performance using 3k samples. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets failures as a gap between apparent semantic understanding and accurate, instance-complete masks. Appendix A.4 interprets the training-size results as saturation at 3k and an optimal cost-performance tradeoff. Section 4.7 also elaborates on frozen SAM's inability to co-adapt and the computational demands of joint optimization.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the retained Seg-Zero comparator as 7B in Tables 1-2, adding model-size information without establishing an actual model change. The main hardware, hyperparameter and preprocessing disclosures are unchanged; no new code-access information or detailed training schedule accompanies the added experiment.

R1.justification: Six cited works are added, including three works supporting a new Section 2.1 sentence about reducing image-specific prompt requirements, plus SOC, visual knowledge graphs and LoRA-Gen. The central positioning relative to LISA, Seg-Zero and VLM-R1 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 moves REC generalization after visualization and ablations, places existing failure ablations in an appendix, and rewrites Broader Impact as Section 4.7. It also updates author-role footnotes and adds acknowledgements. Most introductory, methodological and results prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5 and Table 6, replaces Figure 1's cat example with a camera-focus example, relocates Figure 2 and moves Figure 4 to the appendix. Existing results tables are reordered and renumbered, and Table 1 loses a comparator row. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 makes the final model's segmentation failures concrete, while Table 6 adds useful evidence about the 3k training-data choice. These modestly strengthen the paper's empirical support and limitations analysis. The gains are tempered by removing a Table 1 comparator and asserting saturation and an optimal cost tradeoff from only two sample sizes without uncertainty or measured training costs. The core method and main results remain unchanged.
